lead: Transmission parameters describe a two-port from the input side: they give the input voltage and current in terms of the output voltage and the current leaving port 2. The matrix is also called the chain or ABCD matrix. It exists because cascaded blocks are common: in a receiver chain, a filter followed by an amplifier, you can multiply the matrices instead of re-solving the whole circuit. Some syllabi call these transmission or chain parameters.
prereq: You need: Chapter 6.1 for port variables, 6.2 for the matrix idea, and Unit 1 for KVL and KCL.

sections.h3: The chain relation and its sign convention

blocks.text: A two-port has four external variables: V1, I1, V2 and I2. The ABCD set chooses V2 and the current leaving port 2 as the independent pair. To keep I2 defined as entering port 2, that leaving current is −I2. The relation is:

blocks.where: V1 is the port-1 voltage in V; I1 is the current entering port 1 in A; V2 is the port-2 voltage in V; I2 is the current entering port 2 in A; A, B, C and D are the transmission parameters.

blocks.text: The matrix equation means V1 = A V2 + B(−I2) and I1 = C V2 + D(−I2). Every term is a phasor or a real number; the same equations work for AC at one frequency.

A and D are dimensionless because they relate a voltage to a voltage or a current to a current. B has ohms because it relates a voltage to a current. C has siemens because it relates a current to a voltage.
Each parameter is found by forcing one output condition: open circuit (I2 = 0) or short circuit (V2 = 0). This is why the definitions are called open-circuit and short-circuit parameters.

items: Set I2 = 0, so port 2 is open. Then A = V1/V2 and C = I1/V2.
Set V2 = 0, so port 2 is short. Then B = V1/(−I2) and D = I1/(−I2).
Record the units: A and D are dimensionless; B is in ohms; C is in siemens.
For a reciprocal network, AD − BC = 1; for a symmetric network, A = D.

blocks.text: Reciprocity and symmetry are separate tests. A reciprocal network can be unsymmetric, so AD − BC = 1 may hold while A is not equal to D. A symmetric network has A = D, but reciprocity still needs its own check.

blocks.where: The first condition marks a reciprocal two-port; the second marks a symmetric two-port. A and D are dimensionless, B is in ohms and C is in siemens.

blocks.text: The main reason for ABCD parameters is cascade. Connect port 2 of the first network to port 1 of the second. The output variables of the first become the input variables of the second, so the matrices multiply in signal order.

blocks.where: ABCD1 is the matrix of the block nearest port 1; ABCD2 is the matrix of the block nearest port 2. Multiplication is ordinary matrix multiplication, not element by element.

items: Write each block as [[A, B], [C, D]] with its own values.
Multiply in signal order: first block on the left, second on the right.
Compute A = A1A2 + B1C2, B = A1B2 + B1D2, C = C1A2 + D1C2, D = C1B2 + D1D2.
Check AD − BC = 1 if the total network is reciprocal.

blocks.text: Swapping the order gives a different matrix unless the two blocks are identical or commute. In a cascade, order is part of the circuit.

figure.caption: Two blocks in signal order: the first matrix is nearest port 1 and the second is nearest port 2. The cascade matrix is the product ABCD1 × ABCD2.

spec.aria: In a cascade the chain matrices multiply from left to right.

examples.question: Two two-ports are cascaded in signal order. The first has A1 = 2, B1 = 3 Ω, C1 = 1 S, D1 = 2. The second has A2 = 1, B2 = 0 Ω, C2 = 0.5 S, D2 = 1. Find the overall ABCD matrix. Also verify reciprocity of the cascade.
steps: Check reciprocity: AD − BC = 3.5×2 − 3×2 = 7 − 6 = 1. Both blocks are reciprocal, so the cascade is reciprocal.
examples.answer: ABCD = [[3.5, 3 Ω], [2 S, 2]]; the cascade is reciprocal because AD − BC = 1.

traps: The minus sign on I2 is part of the convention. If you keep I2 as entering port 2 but drop the minus sign and write [V1; I1] = [[A, B], [C, D]][V2; I2], then B and D change sign. Drawing I2 as leaving port 2 and writing the equation with +I2 leaves the values of A, B, C, D unchanged.
Matrix multiplication order matters. ABCD1 × ABCD2 is not the same as ABCD2 × ABCD1 in general.
Do not swap the units: B is an impedance in ohms, while C is an admittance in siemens.
Open and short conditions get mixed up. A and C use I2 = 0 (open output); B and D use V2 = 0 (short output).
AD − BC = 1 tests reciprocity, not symmetry. Symmetry is A = D, and the two tests can pass or fail independently.

quiz.q: Write the defining ABCD matrix equation with the standard sign convention.
quiz.a: [V1; I1] = [[A, B], [C, D]] [V2; −I2], where I2 enters port 2.

quiz.q: Why does the ABCD definition use −I2 instead of I2?
quiz.a: I2 is defined as entering port 2, but the chain relation uses the current leaving port 2. The leaving current is −I2, so the minus sign keeps the port convention consistent.

quiz.q: Give the units of A, B, C and D.
quiz.a: A and D are dimensionless; B is in ohms; C is in siemens.

quiz.q: A two-port has A = 2, B = 3 Ω, C = 1 S, D = 2. Find V1 and I1 when V2 = 10 V and I2 = 0.
At V2 = 0, a two-port has I2 = −2 A, V1 = 6 V and I1 = 4 A. Find B and D.
Two identical reciprocal two-ports, each with A = 2, B = 3 Ω, C = 1 S and D = 2, are cascaded. Find the overall A, B, C and D, and check reciprocity.
A reciprocal two-port has A = 1.5, B = 4 Ω and C = 0.5 S. Find D and state whether the network is symmetric.
quiz.a: From AD − BC = 1: D = (1 + BC)/A = (1 + 4×0.5)/1.5 = 3/1.5 = 2. A = 1.5 and D = 2, so A ≠ D and the network is not symmetric.

beyond: Not for the exam. ABCD matrices are used in RF and microwave design, where filters, amplifiers and transmission-line sections are cascaded on a board. They also appear in power-system transmission-line models and in S-parameter to ABCD conversions for network analysers. In software, tools read Touchstone files and multiply chain matrices to predict a full signal path. Search for ABCD parameters of a transmission line, S to ABCD conversion, and cascaded S-parameters.
